name: Socure first-party suspected-applicant disclosure

attribution.legal_posture: First-party Socure account of an applicant encounter. Socure describes the case as likely tied to a North Korean employment-fraud scam, a suspected probabilistic assessment rather than government attribution, adjudication, confirmed legal identity, or proof that the applicant was hired or caused harm.

caveats: Keep the source label as a label rather than a legal identity or standalone persona; applicant account and private selector details stay outside the record.
DPRK affiliation requires more than nationality, accent, language, appearance, disability, geography, remote-work status, payment method, camera behavior, or any single inconsistency.

Merge the Socure URLs and first-party provenance into the existing context record, preserve the suspected/no-hire boundary, and publish only behavior-level controls. The source label remains contextual; legal identity and standalone persona profile require separate evidence.
This record retains no person, persona, account, organization, image, identity document, biometric artifact, credential, financial selector, device or network selector or private applicant data.
Sources report an attempted scheme; completed impact remains unreported, including hire, payroll entry, corporate access, data loss, theft, extortion, sabotage, and other completed harm.
Suspected or vendor-assessed linkage is an unconfirmed attribution; legal identity, adjudication, and harm require separate evidence.
Socure phrases the DPRK linkage as 'likely tied'; government attribution, adjudicated finding, legal identity, and public technical attribution package status remain unlocated.
The first-party encounter, described screening steps, and no-completion/no-follow-up outcome are Socure's own statements.
Verification noncompletion, interview nonattendance, application inconsistency, geography and other single signals require corroboration before supporting DPRK affiliation or fraud.

infrastructure.statement: Socure says its own recruiting and fraud teams found several fabricated applicants. It describes one applicant that did not complete requested document and live-selfie verification or attend a follow-up interview, and Socure assessed the case as likely tied to a North Korean employment-fraud scam. The sources do not report that the applicant was hired, entered payroll, received corporate access, or caused post-hire harm.
infrastructure.evidence_class: first-party observed applicant case; the encounter and reported outcome are Socure statements, while the DPRK linkage remains Socure-assessed and probabilistic

sources.support: Socure says its recruiters found several fabricated applicants. It describes one applicant that it assessed as likely tied to a North Korean employment-fraud scam; the applicant did not complete requested document and live-selfie verification or attend the follow-up interview. Provenance: The visible page and JSON-LD both provide the 2025-05-29 publication date; JSON-LD provides the 2025-10-16 modification date. The page is the claim-bearing first-party source. sources.locator: Opening through 'Socure vs. Fake Job Applicants'; applicant-pool measurements; applicant comparison; follow-up verification; 'What Employers Should Do'

sources.support: Socure says its solution integrates with HR platforms, job boards, payroll systems, and applicant-tracking systems. It describes identity-risk review at application and ongoing assessment through recruiting, hiring, and onboarding, and it restates the probabilistic assessment of the same applicant encounter. Provenance: The release has a visible July 16, 2025 dateline and embeds the complete claim-bearing text in first-party page data
sources.locator: Dateline and opening; integration and risk-monitoring paragraphs; Rivka Gewirtz Little quotation; DPRK context paragraph
